title: Entity-Anonymized Context Prompts for Improving Context Faithfulness in Knowledge-Conflict QA

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The purpose of the contribution is to improve the context faithfulness of LLMs in knowledge-conflict QA without requiring additional training. Paper [3] explicitly addresses enhancing LLMs' contextual faithfulness in knowledge-conflict scenarios, stating: "we seek to assess and enhance LLMs' contextual faithfulness in two aspects: knowledge conflict and prediction with abstention." This aligns directly with the stated purpose of the contribution. Paper [4] also focuses on improving context faithfulness, introducing "Context-DPO" as a method to align LLMs for context-faithful responses. Both papers share the same high-level objective of improving context faithfulness in knowledge-conflict scenarios.

### Mechanism
The mechanism, Entity-Anonymized Context Prompts (EACP), involves replacing named-entity surface forms with placeholders and an entity inventory, followed by inverse mapping for evaluation. Paper [16] describes a similar mechanism of "entity anonymization" to improve LLMs' attachment to external knowledge in dialogue generation tasks, stating: "we observe that LLMs often rely on internal knowledge, leading to detachment from provided knowledge graphs... we propose anonymizing entities to address this issue." Paper [25] also describes pseudonymization of named entities by replacing them with synthetic surrogates, which is conceptually equivalent to anonymization via placeholders. Both papers employ the same underlying primitive of entity anonymization to address related challenges.

### Evaluation
The evaluation design involves measuring context-faithful rate (Pc) and memorization ratio on a benchmark (ConFiQA-MC) using a specific LLM (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct). Paper [4] introduces the ConFiQA benchmark, which is explicitly used in this contribution, and evaluates context-faithfulness using similar metrics. Paper [18] measures memorization in LLMs, using log-linear relationships to quantify memorization, which aligns with the memorization ratio metric used here. Thus, the evaluation design is covered by prior work.

### Domain
The domain is retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for knowledge-conflict question answering. Paper [6] addresses question answering under contradicting contexts, explicitly dealing with knowledge conflicts in QA. Paper [14] also focuses on open-domain QA with conflicting contexts, introducing a dataset (QACC) to study the problem. Both papers operate in the same general application area of knowledge-conflict QA within RAG.
